q: What is the capital of Australia?
explain: Canberra was purpose-built as the capital as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne.

q: How many planets are in our solar system?
explain: Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006, leaving 8.

q: Which gas do plants absorb from the air?
explain: Plants take in CO2 during photosynthesis and release oxygen.

q: What is the largest ocean on Earth?
explain: The Pacific covers roughly a third of the Earth's surface.

q: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
explain: Leonardo painted it in the early 1500s; it hangs in the Louvre.

q: In which year did World War II end?
explain: Germany surrendered in May 1945 and Japan in September 1945.

q: Which country is the largest by land area?
explain: Russia spans about 17 million km² — nearly twice Canada's area.

q: Roughly how fast does light travel?
explain: About 299,792 km per second — around the Earth 7.5 times in one second.

q: What is the hardest natural substance on Earth?
explain: Diamond scores a 10 on the Mohs hardness scale.

q: How many sides does a hexagon have?
explain: Hexa = six, as in hexagon and hexameter.

q: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
explain: Mars looks red because of iron oxide — rust — on its surface.

q: At what temperature does water freeze?
explain: 0°C = 32°F at normal pressure.

q: What is the tallest mountain on Earth?
explain: Everest is 8,849 m above sea level.

q: Which continent has the most countries?
explain: Africa has 54 recognized countries — more than any other continent.

q: What does DNA stand for?
explain: DNA = deoxyribonucleic acid, the molecule that carries genetic instructions.

q: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
explain: Neil Armstrong stepped onto the Moon on 20 July 1969, followed by Buzz Aldrin.

q: Which language has the most native speakers?
explain: Mandarin has roughly 900+ million native speakers.

q: What is the largest animal that has ever lived?
explain: Blue whales can reach 30 metres and weigh up to 180 tonnes — bigger than any dinosaur we know of.

q: What is the currency of Japan?
explain: Japan uses the yen (¥).

q: How many minutes are there in one day?
explain: 24 hours × 60 minutes = 1440.

q: Which chemical element has the symbol O?
explain: O is oxygen — about 21% of the air we breathe.

q: What is the capital of Spain?
explain: Madrid, right in the centre of the country.

q: Who wrote 'Romeo and Juliet'?
explain: Shakespeare wrote it in the 1590s.

q: In which sport do players hit a shuttlecock?
explain: Badminton uses a feathered shuttlecock; tennis uses a ball.

q: What is the tallest land animal?
explain: Giraffes grow to about 5.5 metres.

q: Which sea is the saltiest on Earth?
explain: The Dead Sea is about 10× saltier than the ocean — you float without trying.

q: How many players are on a football (soccer) team on the pitch?
explain: 11 per side: 10 outfield players plus a goalkeeper.

q: What is the smallest country in the world?
explain: Vatican City covers only 0.44 km².

q: Which instrument has 88 keys?
explain: The standard piano: 52 white keys and 36 black keys.

q: What do bees collect from flowers?
explain: Nectar becomes honey; pollen feeds the hive.
